Has anyone had a physician you pay as a concierge health advisor outside of traditional care? 
I’m wondering if anyone has hired a doctor just to help think through complex health issues (for those that have a complex chronic illness) like reviewing records, giving advice, helping coordinate between specialists… but not as the treating doctor.

So not quite concierge primary care, but more like having someone in the background who knows your case and gives expert input when needed. 

Have you done this? Did it help? How was it set up? When my mom was going through cancer treatment I had a well respected specialist on the other side of the country coordinating her care because she wouldn’t travel.

I made sure to talk to her primary first, but he was fine with it once I made introductions.

I’m not sure why you would do this for primary care unless you have a need for someone highly specialized in a specific illness though.

If you’re having an issue with your concierge doctor I’d look at new groups unless they have other physicians.
